source.text: Ἤδη δὲ τῆς ἑορτῆς μεσούσης ἀνέβη Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἐδίδασκεν.

records.literal_gloss: Already but of the feast being at [its] middle went up Jesus into the temple and was teaching.

en.L: Now when the feast was already at its middle, Jesus went up into the temple and was teaching.
en.B: When the festival was already half over, Jesus went up to the temple courts and began to teach.
en.R: When the festival was about half over, Jesus went up to the temple courts and began to teach there.

es.L: Y cuando ya estaba a la mitad la fiesta, subió Jesús al templo y enseñaba.
es.B: Cuando la fiesta ya iba por la mitad, Jesús subió a los atrios del templo y comenzó a enseñar.
es.R: Cuando la fiesta iba más o menos por la mitad, Jesús subió al patio del templo y comenzó a enseñar allí.

fr.L: Or, la fête étant déjà à [son] milieu, Jésus monta au temple et enseignait.
fr.B: La fête était déjà à moitié passée quand Jésus monta à la cour du temple et se mit à enseigner.
fr.R: La fête était à peu près à moitié passée quand Jésus est monté à la cour du temple. Il a commencé à y enseigner.

sw.L: Basi sikukuu ilipokuwa imefika katikati, Yesu alipanda kwenda hekaluni, akawa anafundisha.
sw.B: Sikukuu ilipokuwa imekwisha fika nusu, Yesu alipanda kwenda kwenye nyua za hekalu, akaanza kufundisha.
sw.R: Sikukuu ilipokuwa karibu nusu, Yesu alipanda kwenda kwenye uwanja wa hekalu, akaanza kufundisha huko.

vi.L: Bấy giờ, khi kỳ lễ đã đến giữa chừng, Đức Giê-xu lên đền thờ và giảng dạy.
vi.B: Khi kỳ lễ đã qua được một nửa, Đức Giê-xu lên sân đền thờ và bắt đầu giảng dạy.
vi.R: Khi kỳ lễ đã qua khoảng một nửa, Đức Giê-xu lên sân đền thờ và bắt đầu giảng dạy ở đó.

ko.L: 그런데 명절이 벌써 중간에 이르렀을 때, 예수께서 성전에 올라가 가르치고 계셨다.
ko.B: 명절이 벌써 절반쯤 지났을 때, 예수께서 성전 뜰에 올라가서 가르치기 시작하셨다.
ko.R: 명절이 반쯤 지났을 때, 예수께서 성전 뜰에 올라가셔서 그곳에서 가르치기 시작하셨다.

pt.L: E, estando a festa já pelo meio, Jesus subiu ao templo e ensinava.
pt.B: Quando a festa já estava pela metade, Jesus subiu aos pátios do templo e começou a ensinar.
pt.R: Quando a festa estava mais ou menos na metade, Jesus foi aos pátios do templo e começou a ensinar ali.

am.L: በዓሉም አሁን እኩሌታ ላይ ሳለ ኢየሱስ ወደ ቤተ መቅደስ ወጣ፤ ያስተምርም ነበር።
am.B: በዓሉ ግማሽ ላይ በደረሰ ጊዜ ኢየሱስ ወደ ቤተ መቅደሱ አደባባይ ወጥቶ ማስተማር ጀመረ።
am.R: በዓሉ ግማሽ ያህል ሲሆን ኢየሱስ ወደ ቤተ መቅደሱ አደባባይ ወጣ፤ በዚያም ማስተማር ጀመረ።

hi.L: जब पर्व आधा बीत चुका था, तब यीशु मन्दिर में ऊपर गए और सिखा रहे थे।
hi.B: जब त्योहार आधा बीत चुका था, तब यीशु मन्दिर के आँगन में गए और सिखाने लगे।
hi.R: जब त्योहार लगभग आधा बीत गया था, तब यीशु मन्दिर के आँगन में गए और वहाँ सिखाने लगे।

ru.L: Когда же праздник был уже в середине, Иисус поднялся в Храм и учил.
ru.B: Когда праздник уже перевалил за половину, Иисус пришёл во двор Храма и начал учить.
ru.R: Когда прошла примерно половина праздника, Иисус пришёл во двор Храма и начал там учить.

uk.L: А коли вже була половина свята, Ісус піднявся до храму і навчав.
uk.B: Коли вже минула половина свята, Ісус піднявся на подвірʼя храму і почав навчати.
uk.R: Коли минуло десь пів свята, Ісус пішов на подвірʼя храму і почав там навчати.

ja.L: さて、祭りがすでに半ばになったころ、イエスは神殿に上って行かれ、教えておられた。
ja.B: 祭りもすでに半ばになったころ、イエスは神殿の境内に上って行き、教え始められた。
ja.R: 祭りが半分ほど過ぎたころ、イエスは神殿の境内に行かれ、そこで教え始められました。

id.L: Ketika hari raya itu sudah berlangsung setengahnya, Yesus naik ke Bait Allah dan mengajar.
id.B: Ketika hari raya itu sudah setengah jalan, Yesus pergi ke halaman Bait Allah dan mulai mengajar.
id.R: Ketika hari raya itu sudah berlangsung kira-kira setengahnya, Yesus pergi ke halaman Bait Allah dan mulai mengajar di sana.

decisions.choice: the middle of the feast: about halfway through the Festival of Tabernacles
decisions.reason: The festival is Tabernacles (7:2), which lasted seven days, with a solemn assembly on the eighth (Leviticus 23:34-36; Deuteronomy 16:13-15). Halfway through would be about the fourth day. Jesus had come up to Jerusalem quietly (7:10); now he teaches in public, in the place where the crowds gathered, while the authorities are looking for him (7:11).

decisions.choice: the temple: the whole temple area with its courts
decisions.reason: John has two words for the temple. This one covers the whole complex, with its open courts and colonnades where teachers taught and crowds could gather (10:23; 18:20). The sanctuary, which only priests entered, has a different word (2:19-21).

decisions.choice: was teaching: began to teach and went on teaching
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes teaching that went on over time. John gives none of the content here; the next verses report what people made of it.

decisions.choice: temple courts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the courts, so that no reader pictures Jesus inside the sanctuary (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the single word, as it does throughout John.

decisions.choice: the festival was half over (B); about half over (R)
alternatives: the feast being in the middle (Literal)
decisions.reason: Everyday English for the middle of a festival of several days; "festival" is the ordinary word for a feast day of this kind, as at 5:1.

decisions.choice: los atrios del templo (B); el patio del templo (R)
decisions.reason: The 2:14 choice for this word, the whole temple area (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense where he uses it; passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (7:14-24), as in 1:19. The passé simple ("monta", "répondit") is the normal tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé ("est monté", "a répondu"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("j’ai fait", "Moïse vous a donné"). The imperfect ("enseignait", "s’étonnaient") is used for what was going on (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: le temple (L); la cour du temple (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word for the whole temple area (meaning decision m2), as at 2:14: Balanced and Readable name the court so that no reader pictures Jesus inside the sanctuary. Literal keeps the single word.

decisions.choice: "성전" (L); "성전 뜰" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word here is the whole temple area with its courts, where people gathered and Jesus taught, not the sanctuary building; Balanced and Readable say "성전 뜰" so the reader does not picture him inside the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun span in Amharic
alternatives: A span like the English one
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Amharic, and the Amharic text of this passage has no such spans (docs/amharic-style.md section 7).

decisions.choice: "ቤተ መቅደስ" (temple) at Literal; "የቤተ መቅደሱ አደባባይ" (the temple courts) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: This word is the whole temple area with its courts (m2), where teachers taught, not the sanctuary itself; Balanced and Readable say so, as the English does and as Matthew 21:12 does in Amharic (docs/john-terms.md: temple words).

decisions.choice: "मन्दिर" (L); "मन्दिर के आँगन" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means the whole temple area with its courts (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say so, as the book's terms set, so no reader pictures Jesus inside the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: "в Храм" (L); "во двор Храма" (B, R)
decisions.reason: This word means the whole temple area with its courts (meaning decision m2); the book's terms keep "temple" at Literal and name the courts at Balanced and Readable, so that no reader pictures Jesus inside the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans for every pronoun for Jesus or God in this passage, "я" and "ты" included; reflexives and a sentence-initial pronoun plain
decisions.reason: As in English, every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting (style guide, sections 7 and 7b).

decisions.choice: "神殿" (L); "神殿の境内" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book's terms: this word is the whole temple area with its courts (m2), so Balanced and Readable say "神殿の境内"; "神殿" alone is kept for the sanctuary (2:19-21). Literal writes "神殿".

source.text: ἐθαύμαζον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι λέγοντες· Πῶς οὗτος γράμματα οἶδεν μὴ μεμαθηκώς;

records.literal_gloss: Were marveling therefore the Jews saying, "How this [man] letters knows not having learned?"

en.L: So the Jews were marveling, saying, "How does this [man] know letters, not having studied?"
en.B: The Jewish leaders were amazed and asked, "How does this man know the Scriptures when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has never studied under a teacher?"
en.R: The Jewish leaders were amazed. "This man never studied with any teacher," they said. "How does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} know so much about the Scriptures?"

es.L: Se maravillaban, pues, los judíos, diciendo: «¿Cómo sabe este letras, sin haber estudiado?».
es.B: Los dirigentes judíos se asombraban y preguntaban: «¿Cómo conoce este las Escrituras sin haber estudiado con un maestro?».
es.R: Los dirigentes judíos estaban asombrados. «Este hombre nunca estudió con ningún maestro», decían. «¿Cómo sabe tanto de las Escrituras?».

fr.L: Les Juifs s’étonnaient donc, disant : « Comment celui-ci connaît-il les lettres, sans avoir étudié ? »
fr.B: Les chefs juifs, étonnés, demandaient : « Comment cet homme connaît-il les Écritures, alors qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a jamais étudié auprès d’un maître ? »
fr.R: Les chefs juifs étaient étonnés. « Cet homme n’a jamais étudié avec un maître, disaient-ils. Comment peut-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} en savoir autant sur les Écritures ? »

sw.L: Basi Wayahudi walikuwa wakishangaa, wakisema, "Huyu anajuaje elimu, hali hajasoma?"
sw.B: Viongozi wa Wayahudi walishangaa, wakauliza, "Mtu huyu anayajuaje Maandiko, wakati hajawahi kusoma chini ya mwalimu?"
sw.R: Viongozi wa Wayahudi walishangaa. "Mtu huyu hajawahi kusoma kwa mwalimu yeyote," wakasema. "Anajuaje mambo mengi hivi ya Maandiko?"

vi.L: Vậy người Do Thái lấy làm lạ và nói: "Sao người này thông chữ nghĩa mà chưa từng học?"
vi.B: Các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái ngạc nhiên hỏi: "Người này chưa từng theo học thầy nào, sao lại hiểu biết Kinh Thánh như vậy?"
vi.R: Các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái rất ngạc nhiên. Họ nói: "Người này chưa bao giờ học với thầy nào. Sao ông ta biết nhiều về Kinh Thánh đến thế?"

ko.L: 그러자 유대인들이 놀라며 말하고 있었다. "이 [사람은] 배우지 않았는데 어떻게 글을 아느냐?"
ko.B: 유대 지도자들은 놀라서 말했다. "이 사람은 스승 밑에서 배운 적도 없는데, 어떻게 성경을 아느냐?"
ko.R: 유대 지도자들은 깜짝 놀라서 말했다. "이 사람은 어떤 선생에게서도 배운 적이 없다. 그런데 어떻게 성경을 이렇게 잘 아느냐?"

pt.L: Então os judeus se admiravam, dizendo: "Como este [homem] conhece as letras, sem ter estudado?"
pt.B: Os líderes judeus ficaram admirados e perguntaram: "Como este homem conhece as Escrituras, se nunca estudou com um mestre?"
pt.R: Os líderes judeus ficaram espantados. "Este homem nunca estudou com nenhum mestre", diziam eles. "Como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} sabe tanto sobre as Escrituras?"

am.L: ስለዚህ አይሁድ እንዲህ እያሉ ይደነቁ ነበር፦ «ይህ [ሰው] ሳይማር ፊደልን እንዴት ያውቃል?»
am.B: የአይሁድ መሪዎችም ተደንቀው እንዲህ ብለው ጠየቁ፦ «ይህ ሰው ከመምህር ሳይማር መጻሕፍትን እንዴት ያውቃል?»
am.R: የአይሁድ መሪዎች ተደነቁ። «ይህ ሰው ከማንም መምህር ዘንድ ተምሮ አያውቅም» አሉ። «ታዲያ መጻሕፍትን ይህን ያህል እንዴት ያውቃል?»

hi.L: तब यहूदी अचंभा करके कहने लगे, "यह [मनुष्य] बिना सीखे विद्या कैसे जानता है?"
hi.B: यहूदी अगुवे चकित होकर पूछने लगे, "इस आदमी ने किसी गुरु से शिक्षा नहीं पाई, तो यह पवित्रशास्त्र को कैसे जानता है?"
hi.R: यहूदी अगुवे हैरान थे। "इस आदमी ने कभी किसी गुरु से नहीं पढ़ा," उन्होंने कहा। "फिर इसे पवित्रशास्त्र की इतनी जानकारी कैसे है?"

ru.L: Итак, иудеи удивлялись, говоря: «Как этот [человек] сведущ в письменах, не учившись?»
ru.B: Иудейские власти изумлялись и спрашивали: «Откуда этот человек знает Писания, если {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} никогда не учился у учителя?»
ru.R: Иудейские вожди удивлялись. «Этот человек никогда не учился у учителя», — говорили они. — «Откуда {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} так много знает о Писаниях?»

uk.L: Тож юдеї дивувалися, кажучи: «Як цей знає письмена, не вчившись?»
uk.B: Представники юдейської влади дивувалися й питали: «Звідки цей чоловік знає Писання, коли {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} ніколи не навчався в учителя?»
uk.R: Юдейські провідники були вражені. «Цей чоловік ніколи не вчився в жодного вчителя», — казали вони. — «Звідки {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} так добре знає Писання?»

ja.L: そこでユダヤ人たちは驚いて言っていた。「どうしてこの者は、学んだこともないのに、文字を知っているのか？」
ja.B: ユダヤ人の指導者たちは驚いて言った。「この男は師について学んだこともないのに、どうして聖書をこれほど知っているのか？」
ja.R: ユダヤ人の指導者たちはびっくりしました。「この男は、先生について学んだことがない」と彼らは言いました。「それなのに、どうして聖書のことをこんなによく知っているのか？」

id.L: Lalu orang-orang Yahudi heran dan berkata, "Bagaimana orang ini mengenal kitab-kitab, padahal {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} tidak pernah belajar?"
id.B: Para pemimpin Yahudi heran dan bertanya, "Bagaimana orang ini bisa mengerti Kitab Suci, padahal {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} tidak pernah berguru?"
id.R: Para pemimpin Yahudi heran. "Orang ini tidak pernah belajar pada seorang guru," kata mereka. "Bagaimana {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} bisa tahu begitu banyak tentang Kitab Suci?"

decisions.choice: the Jews: most likely the religious authorities in Jerusalem
alternatives: the Jewish people at the festival in general
decisions.reason: In this chapter the word first means the authorities: they want to kill Jesus (7:1), they look for him at the festival (7:11), and the crowd is afraid of them (7:13). Jesus answers these people (7:16) and asks why they are trying to kill him (7:19); the crowd, which knows nothing of a plot, then speaks up separately (7:20). The other reading is possible, since Jesus is teaching in public and anyone could have been amazed. A footnote gives it.

decisions.choice: letters: learning, especially in the Scriptures
alternatives: the ability to read and write
decisions.reason: The word means the letters of the alphabet, and from that, writings and learning. Jesus is teaching in the temple, so the question is how he knows the Scriptures and their meaning well enough to teach them. Moses' "writings" are called by the same word in 5:47. The question is not whether he can read.

decisions.choice: not having studied: not trained under a recognized teacher
decisions.reason: A teacher of the law was expected to have studied for years with a known rabbi and to pass on what he had received. Jesus had no such teacher (compare Acts 4:13 of Peter and John). The next verse answers this exactly: Jesus does have a teacher, the one who sent him.

decisions.choice: were marveling ... this [man]: astonishment with an edge of disapproval
decisions.reason: The same verb can describe admiration or shocked surprise (5:28; 7:21). Here "this man", said without his name, and the rest of the scene suggest the authorities are puzzled and suspicious rather than won over.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: The book-wide rule for John: Literal always says "the Jews"; Balanced and Readable name the group meant, here the authorities (meaning decision m1). A footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: the Scriptures (B, R); under a teacher (B); with any teacher (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of learning is meant and what kind of study was expected (meaning decisions m2 and m3). Readable puts the fact first and the question second, to keep each sentence short.

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los dirigentes judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the religious authorities in Jerusalem (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable name them, as at 5:10-18. The word John wrote is "los judíos".

decisions.choice: las Escrituras; con un maestro
decisions.reason: As in English: says what kind of learning and study is meant (meaning decisions m2, m3). Literal keeps "saber letras", which is a Spanish idiom too.

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); les chefs juifs (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John, first used here in this passage. Literal keeps the word John wrote. Balanced and Readable name the group the context most likely shows, the religious authorities in Jerusalem (meaning decision m1); in French "les Juifs" alone reads as the whole people, and Jesus too is a Jew. The footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: "유대인들" (L); "유대 지도자들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Where John means the authorities in Jerusalem, Balanced and Readable name them; Literal keeps the word John wrote. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the reader setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus is carried by the subject honorific ("-시-", "께서") and "그분" in the narrative at every level. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: người Do Thái (L); các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái (B, R)
alternatives: người Do Thái at every level
decisions.reason: As the guide sets for the whole book: where John means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: thông chữ nghĩa
decisions.reason: "biết chữ" would mean only "can read"; "chữ nghĩa" is book learning, which is what "letters" means here.

decisions.choice: "አይሁድ" (L); "የአይሁድ መሪዎች" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Most likely the religious authorities in Jerusalem are meant (m1, uncertain), as in 7:1-13, so Balanced and Readable name them, as the English does (docs/john-terms.md); Literal keeps the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: "ፊደልን" (letters) at Literal; "መጻሕፍትን" (the Scriptures) at Balanced and Readable

decisions.choice: my teaching is not mine: Jesus does have a teacher, God who sent him
decisions.reason: This answers the charge that he never studied (7:15). The teaching is his because he gives it, but its source is the Father. John returns to this again and again: the Son does nothing on his own (5:19, 30), and speaks what the Father taught him (8:28; 12:49-50).

decisions.choice: them: the people who asked the question in 7:15
decisions.reason: The pronoun picks up the speakers of the previous verse. What follows, up to 7:19, is said to them.

decisions.choice: the one who sent me: God, described by his act of sending
decisions.reason: Jesus often speaks of God in John as "the one who sent me" (4:34; 5:24, 30; 6:38-39). A messenger's words carry the authority of the one who sends him.

decisions.choice: two sentences: not my own ... It comes from ...
alternatives: My teaching is not mine but his who sent me
decisions.reason: The Greek plays on "my" and "mine". Balanced and Readable split the contrast into two sentences so the paradox reads clearly without sounding like a contradiction.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: As in English: the paradox reads more clearly split. "Mía" (a possessive) takes no setting, as elsewhere in Spanish.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체: "것이다", "느냐")
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the whole book, Jesus speaks to crowds and opponents in 해라체; Readable uses plainer words, not a softer speech level. God, "the one who sent me", takes the honorific ("보내신 분"). This holds for the passage.

decisions.choice: Đấng đã sai Ta
decisions.reason: "Đấng" is the respectful word for a divine person; the Greek names God by his act of sending, and "Đấng đã sai Ta" keeps that without naming him. Used through the book.

uk.R: Хто справді хоче робити те, чого хоче Бог, той дізнається, чи те, чого {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} навчаю, походить від Бога, чи {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} просто говорю від себе.

ja.L: もしだれかがその方の御心を行うことを望むなら、その人はその教えについて、それが神から出たものか、それともわたしが自分から語っているのか、知るであろう。
ja.B: その方の御心を行おうと心に決めている人は、この教えが神から出たものか、それともわたしが自分の権威で語っているのか、分かるはずだ。
ja.R: 神が望んでおられることを本当に行いたいと思う人は、わたしが教えていることが神から出たものか、それとも、わたしがただ自分の考えを話しているだけなのか、分かるようになる。

id.L: jika seseorang mau melakukan kehendak-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, ia akan mengetahui tentang ajaran itu, apakah berasal dari Allah atau {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} berbicara dari diri-{{deity_pronoun:ku|Ku}} sendiri.
id.B: Kalau seseorang sungguh mau melakukan kehendak-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, ia akan tahu apakah ajaran ini berasal dari Allah atau {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} berbicara atas kehendak-{{deity_pronoun:ku|Ku}} sendiri.
id.R: Siapa saja yang sungguh-sungguh mau melakukan apa yang dikehendaki Allah akan tahu apakah ajaran-{{deity_pronoun:ku|Ku}} berasal dari Allah, atau {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} hanya berbicara atas nama diri-{{deity_pronoun:ku|Ku}} sendiri.

decisions.choice: wills to do his will: a settled choice to obey God, not only a wish
alternatives: happens to do what God wants
decisions.reason: The sentence uses the verb "to will" and the noun "will" side by side. The condition is the person's own intent to do what God wants. "His" is the one who sent Jesus (7:16).

decisions.choice: knowing the source of the teaching follows a willingness to obey God
alternatives: learning more facts settles the question
decisions.reason: Jesus does not offer credentials to answer 7:15. He says that someone who wants to do God's will is able to recognize God's teaching when they hear it (compare 8:47; 10:4).

decisions.choice: I speak from myself: I speak on my own authority, as my own source
decisions.reason: The phrase is used in John for acting or speaking as one's own source rather than as one sent (5:19, 30; 7:28; 14:10). It is the opposite of what 7:16 has just said.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: "Anyone" includes men and women, so the pronoun that picks it up follows the gender setting.

decisions.choice: what God wants
decisions.reason: Readable names God instead of using a pronoun whose referent is a verse back (7:16).

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: Spanish needs no pronoun for "anyone" ("conocerá", "sabrá"), so no setting applies.

decisions.choice: por mi propia cuenta (B); por mi cuenta (R); por mí mismo (L)
decisions.reason: As at 5:19 and 5:30 (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: no gender setting: "il" after "quelqu’un" (L); "Celui qui" (B, R)
decisions.reason: English puts "they/he" under the gender setting. In French "il" taking up the indefinite "quelqu’un" is the grammatical agreement and is read as "anyone", and Balanced and Readable avoid the pronoun with "celui qui", the usual general form, as Spanish avoids it. A doubled "il ou elle" would be heavy in a sentence that is about anyone at all.

decisions.choice: no gender spans in this chapter
decisions.reason: The English needs "they" with "he" as the traditional alternative. Swahili "mtu yeyote" and its verbs (a-tajua) say nothing about sex, so there is nothing for the setting to change here or in verses 18, 37, 46 and 51.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "누구든지 ... 사람은"
alternatives: a gender setting span as in English
decisions.reason: Korean needs no pronoun after "누구든지" (anyone), so there is nothing for the gender setting to change; the sentence already includes everyone.

decisions.choice: "ai ... người ấy", with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: "ai" (anyone) and "người ấy" (that person) are already inclusive, so the gender setting has nothing to change here or in verse 18.

decisions.choice: alguém ... saberá, with no gender setting
alternatives: a gender setting on a pronoun
decisions.reason: Portuguese leaves the subject of "saberá" ("conhecerá") unexpressed, so there is no pronoun to choose and "alguém" already means anyone; the English "they/he" setting has nothing to attach to (style section 7).

decisions.choice: No gender span on "they/he" and "their/his" in 7:17-18
decisions.reason: The Amharic verb endings and "ራሱ" (himself) used here are the generic ones for anyone, man or woman, and "ማንም" (anyone) is already inclusive, so the gender setting has nothing to change (docs/amharic-style.md section 7b).

decisions.choice: "वह", "अपनी", no gender span
decisions.reason: The English has gender spans on the pronouns for "anyone" here and in 7:18. Hindi "वह" and "अपना" mean he or she, and the generic masculine verb is ordinary Hindi, so no span is needed.

decisions.choice: no gender span (L: no pronoun; B: "он" for "кто-то")
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span for the pronoun that picks up "anyone". Russian leaves it out at Literal, and at Balanced the masculine "он" after "кто-то" already covers men and women, so no setting is needed; likewise the reflexives in 7:18.

decisions.choice: "той пізнає", "сам від себе", "власної слави", with no gender setting, here and in verse 18
alternatives: a gender setting, as in the English
decisions.reason: The English needs a gender setting for "they/he" and "their/his". The Ukrainian "хтось ... той" and the reflexive "себе", "власний" already speak of any person, man or woman.

decisions.choice: "その人", "人", "者", "自分" with no gender span (here and in 7:18)
alternatives: a span such as {{gender:その人|彼}}
decisions.reason: The English needs a gender span for its pronouns (they/he). Japanese words for a person are already inclusive, so no span is needed.

decisions.choice: "御心" (L, B); "神が望んでおられること" (R)
decisions.reason: "御心" is the living Japanese word for God's will. Readable says it in everyday words and names God, since "his" points back to the one who sent Jesus (m1).

source.text: ὁ ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ λαλῶν τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἰδίαν ζητεῖ· ὁ δὲ ζητῶν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτὸν οὗτος ἀληθής ἐστιν καὶ ἀδικία ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] from himself speaking the glory the own seeks; the [one] but seeking the glory of the [one] having sent him, this [one] true is and unrighteousness in him not is.

en.L: The one speaking from {{gender:themselves|himself}} seeks {{gender:their|his}} own glory; but the one seeking the glory of the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, this [one] is true, and unrighteousness is not in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Whoever speaks on {{gender:their|his}} own authority is after {{gender:their|his}} own glory. But the one who seeks the glory of the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} is true, and there is nothing false in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: People who speak only for themselves want glory for themselves. But I want glory for the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. So I am telling the truth, and there is nothing false in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: El que habla por su propia cuenta busca su propia gloria; pero el que busca la gloria del que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} envió, este es veraz, y no hay injusticia en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Quien habla por su propia cuenta busca su propia gloria. Pero el que busca la gloria del que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} envió es veraz, y no hay nada falso en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Los que hablan solo por su cuenta buscan gloria para sí mismos. Pero yo busco la gloria del que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió. Por eso digo la verdad, y no hay nada falso en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.L: Celui qui parle par lui-même cherche sa propre gloire ; mais celui qui cherche la gloire de celui qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a envoyé, celui-là est vrai, et il n’y a pas d’injustice en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Celui qui parle de sa propre autorité recherche sa propre gloire. Mais celui qui cherche la gloire de celui qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a envoyé dit la vérité, et il n’y a rien de faux en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Ceux qui parlent seulement en leur propre nom veulent la gloire pour eux-mêmes. Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je veux la gloire pour celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. Alors je dis la vérité, et il n’y a rien de faux en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Yule anayesema kwa nafsi yake hutafuta utukufu wake mwenyewe; lakini yule anayetafuta utukufu wa yule aliyemtuma, huyo ni wa kweli, wala hamna udhalimu ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Yeyote anayesema kwa mamlaka yake mwenyewe hutafuta utukufu wake mwenyewe. Lakini yule anayetafuta utukufu wa aliyemtuma ni wa kweli, wala hakuna uongo ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Watu wanaosema kwa niaba yao wenyewe hutaka utukufu kwa ajili yao wenyewe. Lakini mimi nataka utukufu kwa ajili ya yule aliyenituma. Kwa hiyo nasema kweli, wala hakuna uongo ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

vi.L: Người tự mình nói thì tìm vinh quang cho riêng mình; còn ai tìm vinh quang của Đấng đã sai mình, người ấy là chân thật, và nơi người ấy không có điều bất chính.
vi.B: Ai nói theo ý riêng mình là tìm vinh quang cho chính mình. Nhưng ai tìm vinh quang cho Đấng đã sai mình thì người ấy chân thật, và nơi người ấy không có gì gian dối.
vi.R: Người chỉ nói theo ý mình thì muốn được vinh quang cho chính mình. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} muốn vinh quang thuộc về Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Vì vậy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói thật, và nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không có gì gian dối.

ko.L: 스스로 말하는 사람은 자기 영광을 구한다. 그러나 자기를 보내신 분의 영광을 구하는 사람, 이 사람은 참되고, 그 안에는 불의가 없다.
ko.B: 자기 권위로 말하는 사람은 자기 영광을 구한다. 그러나 자기를 보내신 분의 영광을 구하는 사람은 참되고, 그 안에는 거짓이 없다.
ko.R: 자기 생각만 말하는 사람은 자기가 영광을 받으려고 한다. 그러나 나는 나를 보내신 분이 영광을 받으시기를 바란다. 그러니 나는 진실을 말하고 있고, 내 안에는 거짓이 하나도 없다.

pt.L: Aquele que fala por si mesmo busca a própria glória; mas aquele que busca a glória daquele que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} enviou, este é verdadeiro, e não há injustiça {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}.
pt.B: Quem fala por sua própria autoridade está atrás da própria glória. Mas quem busca a glória daquele que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} enviou é verdadeiro, e não há nada de falso {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}.
pt.R: Quem fala só por si mesmo quer glória para si mesmo. Mas eu quero glória para aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou. Por isso eu estou dizendo a verdade, e não há nada de falso em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.

am.L: ከራሱ የሚናገር የራሱን ክብር ይፈልጋል፤ የላከውን ክብር የሚፈልግ ግን እርሱ እውነተኛ ነው፤ በእርሱም ዓመፃ የለም።
am.B: በራሱ ሥልጣን የሚናገር የራሱን ክብር ይፈልጋል። የላከውን ክብር የሚፈልግ ግን እውነተኛ ነው፤ በእርሱም ምንም ሐሰት የለም።
am.R: ለራሳቸው ብቻ የሚናገሩ ሰዎች ለራሳቸው ክብር ይፈልጋሉ። እኔ ግን ለላከኝ ክብር እፈልጋለሁ። ስለዚህ እውነትን እናገራለሁ፤ በእኔም ምንም ሐሰት የለም።

hi.L: जो अपनी ओर से बोलता है, वह अपनी ही महिमा चाहता है; पर जो अपने भेजनेवाले की महिमा चाहता है, वही सच्चा है, और उसमें अधर्म नहीं।
hi.B: जो अपने ही अधिकार से बोलता है, वह अपनी महिमा के पीछे रहता है। पर जो अपने भेजनेवाले की महिमा चाहता है, वह सच्चा है, और उसमें कुछ भी झूठ नहीं।
hi.R: जो लोग केवल अपनी ओर से बोलते हैं, वे अपने लिए महिमा चाहते हैं। पर मैं अपने भेजनेवाले के लिए महिमा चाहता हूँ। इसलिए मैं सच बोल रहा हूँ, और मुझमें कुछ भी झूठ नहीं है।

ru.L: Говорящий от себя ищет собственной славы; а ищущий славы пославшего {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} — этот истинен, и неправды в {{deity_pronoun:нём|Нём}} нет.
ru.B: Кто говорит от своего имени, тот добивается собственной славы. А тот, кто ищет славы для того, кто {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} послал, правдив, и в {{deity_pronoun:нём|Нём}} нет ничего ложного.
ru.R: Люди, которые говорят только от себя, хотят славы для себя. Но {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} хочу славы для того, кто {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} послал. Значит, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} говорю правду, и во {{deity_pronoun:мне|Мне}} нет ничего ложного.

uk.L: Хто говорить сам від себе, шукає власної слави; а хто шукає слави того, хто послав {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, той правдивий, і неправедності в {{deity_pronoun:ньому|Ньому}} немає.
uk.B: Хто говорить від себе, той шукає власної слави. Але хто шукає слави того, хто {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} послав, той правдивий, і немає в {{deity_pronoun:ньому|Ньому}} нічого фальшивого.
uk.R: Люди, які говорять лише від себе, хочуть слави для себе. А {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} хочу слави для того, хто {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} послав. Тож {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} кажу правду, і немає в {{deity_pronoun:мені|Мені}} нічого фальшивого.

ja.L: 自分から語る者は、自分自身の栄光を求める。しかし、自分を遣わされた方の栄光を求める者、この者は真実であり、その内には不義がない。
ja.B: 自分の権威で語る者は、自分の栄光を求めている。しかし、自分を遣わされた方の栄光を求める者は真実であって、その人には偽りがない。
ja.R: 自分のためだけに話す人は、自分が栄光を受けることを求めている。しかし、わたしは、わたしを遣わされた方が栄光を受けることを求めている。だから、わたしは本当のことを話しているし、わたしの中にうそは何もない。

id.L: Siapa yang berbicara dari dirinya sendiri, ia mencari hormat bagi dirinya sendiri; tetapi siapa yang mencari hormat bagi {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} yang mengutusnya, dia itu benar dan di dalam dia tidak ada ketidakadilan.
id.B: Siapa yang berbicara atas kehendaknya sendiri mencari hormat bagi dirinya sendiri. Tetapi siapa yang mencari hormat bagi {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} yang mengutusnya, dia itu benar, dan di dalam dirinya tidak ada kepalsuan.
id.R: Orang yang hanya berbicara atas nama dirinya sendiri mencari pujian untuk dirinya sendiri. Tetapi {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} mencari pujian untuk {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} yang mengutus {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}}. Jadi {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} mengatakan yang benar, dan tidak ada kepalsuan di dalam diri-{{deity_pronoun:ku|Ku}}.

decisions.choice: a general saying whose second half describes Jesus himself
alternatives: two general sayings about any teacher
decisions.reason: Both halves are worded as general rules. The first describes any teacher who is his own source. The second fits only the one who has just said that his teaching comes from the one who sent him (7:16), so Jesus is speaking of himself.

decisions.choice: glory: honor and praise
decisions.reason: Here glory is the honor a person seeks or receives. In 5:41-44 Jesus says he does not accept glory from people, and asks how those who receive glory from one another can believe.

decisions.choice: true: truthful and to be trusted
decisions.reason: The adjective describes a person whose word can be relied on (3:33; 8:26). It is not the noun for truth that John uses as a key word.

decisions.choice: unrighteousness: wrongdoing, here especially falseness
decisions.reason: The word means any kind of wrong. Set beside "true", it points to deceit: such a person is not trying to mislead anyone. It is the opposite of what is right, but not the noun for righteousness that is a key term.

decisions.choice: unrighteousness (L); nothing false (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the broad word. Balanced and Readable give the sense this context calls for (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: But I want glory for the one who sent me
alternatives: But whoever seeks the glory of the one who sent him
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the second half is about Jesus (meaning decision m1), and keeps the first half general.

decisions.choice: no gender setting; él for the second half
decisions.reason: "El que habla" and "su" are general in Spanish, so the first half needs no setting. The second half describes Jesus (meaning decision m1), so its stressed "él" takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: injusticia (L); nada falso (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the broad word; Balanced and Readable give the sense here (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: no gender setting in the first half; deity_pronoun on "l’" and "lui" in the second
decisions.reason: As in verse 17. French "sa propre gloire" does not mark gender, and "celui qui ... lui-même" is the general French form; "soi-même" would read as "talks about oneself". The second half describes Jesus (meaning decision m1), so its pronouns take the deity_pronoun setting, as in English.

decisions.choice: "mình", "người ấy" with no deity_pronoun span
alternatives: "Ngài" under the deity_pronoun setting, as the English "him"
decisions.reason: The saying is general in form, and Vietnamese "người ấy" keeps it general; "Ngài" would turn it into a plain statement about Jesus, which only Readable makes explicit ("Ta").

decisions.choice: aquele que / quem fala por si mesmo, with no gender setting
alternatives: a gender setting on the reflexive
decisions.reason: "Quem" and "aquele que" are generic in Portuguese, and "si mesmo" and "a própria glória" do not mark gender, so the English setting on "themselves/himself" and "their/his" is not needed (style section 7).

decisions.choice: "ክብር" (glory) at every level
decisions.reason: Glory is a key term (docs/john-terms.md; docs/amharic-style.md section 6), and keeping "ክብር" here links the honour Jesus does not seek for himself with the glory of 1:14 and of his hour.

decisions.choice: "अधर्म" (L); "कुछ भी झूठ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the broad word; Balanced and Readable give the sense this context calls for, falseness (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: "неправды" (L); "ничего ложного" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the broad word; Balanced and Readable give the sense this context calls for, falseness (meaning decision m4).
Set beside "true", the wrong meant is falseness (m4). Literal keeps the general word "不義"; Balanced and Readable say what kind of wrong it is.

decisions.choice: "mengutusnya", "dia itu", "dirinya" in lowercase, with no deity span
decisions.reason: m1: both halves are worded as general sayings, and the second describes Jesus only by implication. Indonesian has no neutral pronoun that the setting could switch, and the capitalised form would say outright what the saying only implies, so Literal and Balanced keep the lowercase of a general saying. Readable speaks of Jesus directly, as the English Readable does, and takes the spans. "hormat" for glory in the sense of honour, as at 5:41.

source.text: Οὐ Μωϋσῆς δέδωκεν ὑμῖν τὸν νόμον;

records.literal_gloss: Not Moses has given you the law?

en.L: Has not Moses given you the law?
en.B: Did not Moses give you the law?
en.R: Moses gave you the law, did he not?

es.R: Moisés {{plural_you:les|os}} dio la ley, ¿no es así?

decisions.choice: you have a demon: you are out of your mind
alternatives: a careful claim that he is possessed
decisions.reason: To say someone "has a demon" was a common way of calling him mad or raving; the two charges stand side by side in 10:20. It is an insult rather than a diagnosis (compare 8:48, 52).

decisions.choice: the crowd: festival pilgrims who do not know about the plot
decisions.reason: The crowd is different from the people who questioned Jesus. Many had come from elsewhere for the festival and knew nothing of a plan to kill him, so his question sounds absurd to them. Some people of Jerusalem did know of it (7:25).

decisions.choice: who is seeking to kill you?: a denial in the form of a question
decisions.reason: They mean that nobody is trying to kill him. The reader knows better (5:18; 7:1).

decisions.choice: You must have a demon (B); You are out of your mind (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the image with a word that marks it as an outburst. Readable gives what the insult meant (meaning decision m1), since a modern reader might take it as a literal claim of possession.

decisions.choice: ¡Debes de tener un demonio! (B); ¡Estás loco! (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable gives what the insult meant (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: The crowd speaks to Jesus in the plain style ("너", "말이냐")
decisions.reason: The style guide gives 합쇼체 to people speaking to Jesus, but allows plain speech where the scene is hostile. Here the crowd retorts "You have a demon!", a rude outburst; formal politeness would contradict it. A reviewer should judge the level.

decisions.choice: "आपमें दुष्टात्मा है" (L, B); "आपका दिमाग़ ख़राब हो गया है" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the image; Readable gives what the insult meant, that he is out of his mind (meaning decision m1). The crowd still says "आप" to Jesus, as the style guide sets.

decisions.choice: "Бес у тебя" (L); "одержим бесом" (B); "Ты с ума сошёл" (R)
decisions.reason: "You have a demon" was a way of saying "you are out of your mind" (meaning decision m1); Literal and Balanced keep the image, Readable gives what the insult meant.

decisions.choice: "悪霊を持っている" (L); "悪霊に取りつかれている" (B); "頭がおかしい" (R)
alternatives: "気が変になっている" at Balanced
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek's words; Balanced uses the natural Japanese phrase for having a demon; Readable gives what the insult meant, that he is out of his mind (m1). The crowd speaks plainly and rudely to him.

decisions.choice: "kerasukan setan" (L); "kerasukan roh jahat" (B); "sudah gila" (R)
decisions.reason: m1: to "have a demon" was a common way of calling someone mad. The demon words follow the glossary ("setan" at Literal, "roh jahat" at Balanced); Readable gives the sense, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: one work: the healing at the pool of Bethesda on a Sabbath
decisions.reason: Jesus last taught in Jerusalem when he healed the man who had been ill for thirty-eight years, on a Sabbath (5:1-9). That one act started the authorities' plan against him (5:16-18). Verse 23 confirms which work he means. John often calls what Jesus does "works" (5:20, 36; 7:3).

decisions.choice: marvel: amazement mixed with disapproval
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the authorities in 7:15. Here it is the shocked surprise of people who think Jesus broke the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: you all: everyone listening, the crowd and the authorities
decisions.reason: Jesus now answers the crowd that has just spoken (7:20), and includes all who had heard of the healing.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Readable names the day, which Jesus makes explicit in 7:23, so that young readers know which work is meant.

decisions.choice: work

records.literal_gloss: Because of this Moses has given you the circumcision, not that from the Moses it is but from the fathers, and on Sabbath you circumcise a man.

en.L: Because of this Moses has given you circumcision (not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers), and on [the] Sabbath you circumcise a man.
en.B: So consider this: Moses gave you circumcision (though it did not begin with Moses but with the patriarchs), and you circumcise a boy even on the Sabbath.
en.R: So think about this. Moses gave you the command to circumcise baby boys. (It did not really start with Moses. It started long before him, with Abraham and his sons.) And you circumcise a baby boy even on the Sabbath.

fr.R: Alors réfléchissez. Moïse vous a donné l’ordre de circoncire les petits garçons. (En fait, cela n’a pas commencé avec Moïse. Cela a commencé bien avant lui, avec Abraham et ses fils.) Et vous circoncisez un bébé même le jour du sabbat.

id.L: Karena itu Musa telah memberikan sunat kepada kalian, bukan karena sunat itu berasal dari Musa, tetapi dari nenek moyang, dan kalian menyunat seorang manusia pada hari Sabat.
id.B: Jadi, pikirkanlah ini: Musa memberikan sunat kepada kalian (walaupun sunat itu tidak berasal dari Musa, tetapi dari para bapa leluhur), dan kalian menyunat seorang anak laki-laki pada hari Sabat.
id.R: Jadi, pikirkan hal ini. Musa memberi kalian perintah untuk menyunat bayi laki-laki. (Sebenarnya sunat tidak dimulai oleh Musa. Sunat sudah ada jauh sebelum dia, sejak Abraham dan anak-anaknya.) Dan kalian menyunat bayi laki-laki pada hari Sabat juga.

decisions.choice: because of this begins verse 22 and introduces Jesus's answer (SBLGNT)
alternatives: it ends verse 21: you all marvel because of this
decisions.reason: The phrase can be read with the end of 7:21 ("you are all amazed because of it") or with the start of 7:22. The SBLGNT places it at the start of 7:22. Read that way, Jesus turns from their amazement to the case of circumcision, which explains why the healing should not shock them. Elsewhere John nearly always puts this phrase at the start of its sentence (5:16, 18; 6:65), which favors the SBLGNT, but the other reading is old and makes good sense. A footnote gives it.

decisions.choice: circumcision came from the patriarchs, and Moses gave it a place in the law
decisions.reason: God gave circumcision to Abraham as the sign of the covenant, for every male on the eighth day (Genesis 17:10-12), long before Moses. The law of Moses then repeated it (Leviticus 12:3). Jesus corrects his own words in passing, because the age of the command matters to his argument: it is older than the Sabbath law given at Sinai.

decisions.choice: circumcision was performed on the Sabbath when the eighth day fell on it
alternatives: they waited until the Sabbath was over
decisions.reason: When a boy's eighth day was a Sabbath, the circumcision was done that day, even though it was work. Jewish teaching later written down in the Mishnah (tractate Shabbat 18:3 and 19:2) allows this. A reviewer should check these references.

decisions.choice: a man: a human being, here a newborn boy
decisions.reason: The word means a person. Here it is the male child being circumcised on his eighth day; the same word comes back twice in 7:23.

decisions.choice: So consider this (B); So think about this (R)
decisions.reason: Following the SBLGNT, the phrase introduces the argument (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable say so in words that point ahead, since "for this reason Moses gave you circumcision" would suggest a reason the text does not give.

decisions.choice: the patriarchs (B); Abraham and his sons (R); a boy (B); a baby boy (R)
decisions.reason: "The fathers" are Israel's founding ancestors, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Balanced and Readable say who is meant, and say "boy" because circumcision on the eighth day was done to infants. This loses the repetition of "man" in 7:23, which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: Piensen en esto
decisions.reason: As in English: following the SBLGNT, the phrase introduces the argument (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: los patriarcas (B); Abraham y sus hijos (R); un niño (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: says who "the fathers" are, and that the one circumcised is a baby boy (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: phép cắt bì; ngày Sa-bát
decisions.reason: The established Protestant words: "phép cắt bì" for the rite and "ngày Sa-bát" for the Sabbath, which keeps the name rather than explaining it as "the day of rest".

decisions.choice: "कुलपिताओं" (B); "अब्राहम और उसके बेटों" (R); "लड़के" (B, R) for "a man"
decisions.reason: "The fathers" are Israel's founding ancestors, and "a man" here is a newborn boy (meaning decision m4); Balanced and Readable say who is meant, Literal keeps the Greek words.

decisions.choice: "праотцов" (B); "Авраама и его сыновей" (R); "мальчика" (B, R) for "человека"
decisions.reason: "The fathers" are Israel's founding ancestors, and the one circumcised on the eighth day is a newborn boy (meaning decision m4); Literal keeps "отцы" and "человек".

decisions.choice: the aside set off with "――" (L); a sentence of its own (B); in parentheses (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus corrects himself in passing (m2). Literal keeps the aside inside the sentence, marked off by dashes; Balanced makes it a sentence beginning "もっとも"; Readable keeps the English Readable's parentheses.

source.text: εἰ περιτομὴν λαμβάνει ἄνθρωπος ἐν σαββάτῳ ἵνα μὴ λυθῇ ὁ νόμος Μωϋσέως, ἐμοὶ χολᾶτε ὅτι ὅλον ἄνθρωπον ὑγιῆ ἐποίησα ἐν σαββάτῳ;

records.literal_gloss: If circumcision receives a man on Sabbath so that not may be broken the law of Moses, with me are you angry because whole a man well I made on Sabbath?

en.L: If a man receives circumcision on [the] Sabbath so that the law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} because I made a whole man well on [the] Sabbath?
en.B: If a boy is circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses is not broken, why are you angry with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for making a man entirely well on the Sabbath?
en.R: You circumcise a baby boy on the Sabbath so that you do not break the law of Moses. Circumcision deals with only one part of the body. But I made a man well in his whole body on the Sabbath. So why are you angry with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

es.L: Si un hombre recibe la circuncisión en sábado para que no se quebrante la ley de Moisés, ¿{{plural_you:se enojan|os enojáis}} conmigo porque sané por completo a un hombre en sábado?
es.B: Si se circuncida a un niño en sábado para no quebrantar la ley de Moisés, ¿por qué {{plural_you:se enojan|os enojáis}} conmigo por haber sanado por completo a un hombre en sábado?
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes circuncidan|Vosotros circuncidáis}} a un niño en sábado para no desobedecer la ley de Moisés. La circuncisión tiene que ver con una sola parte del cuerpo. Pero yo sané a un hombre en todo su cuerpo en sábado. Entonces, ¿por qué {{plural_you:se enojan|os enojáis}} conmigo?

fr.L: Si un homme reçoit la circoncision [un jour de] sabbat afin que la Loi de Moïse ne soit pas enfreinte, vous irritez-vous contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} parce que j’ai rendu un homme entièrement sain [un jour de] sabbat ?
fr.B: Si l’on circoncit un petit garçon le jour du sabbat pour ne pas enfreindre la Loi de Moïse, pourquoi vous irritez-vous contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} parce que j’ai rendu la santé à un homme tout entier le jour du sabbat ?
fr.R: Vous circoncisez un bébé le jour du sabbat, pour ne pas désobéir à la Loi de Moïse. La circoncision ne concerne qu’une seule partie du corps. Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, j’ai guéri un homme dans tout son corps, le jour du sabbat. Alors pourquoi êtes-vous en colère contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ?

sw.L: Ikiwa mtu hupokea tohara siku ya Sabato ili sheria ya Musa isivunjwe, mbona mnanikasirikia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} kwa sababu nimemfanya mtu mzima kabisa siku ya Sabato?

ru.B: Если мальчика обрезают в субботу, чтобы не нарушить Закон Моисея, почему вы гневаетесь на {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} за то, что {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} сделал человека совершенно здоровым в субботу?

decisions.choice: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If the law allows a small act on the Sabbath to keep the law, it must allow a much greater one. Jewish teachers often argued this way. A later rabbinic saying uses the same comparison: if circumcision, which concerns one part of the body, sets aside the Sabbath, how much more saving a whole life (Babylonian Talmud, Yoma 85b). A reviewer should check this reference.

decisions.choice: so that the law is not broken: so that the eighth-day command is kept
alternatives: so that the Sabbath is not broken
decisions.reason: The law that would be broken is the command to circumcise on the eighth day (Leviticus 12:3). To keep it, they set aside the rest of the Sabbath. So even by their own practice, one command can give way to another.

decisions.choice: a whole man well: the whole person healed, as against one part of the body
decisions.reason: "Whole" sets the healing against circumcision, which concerns one part of the body. The man of 5:1-9 had been ill for thirty-eight years and was made well in every way. "Made well" is the phrase used of him in 5:6-15.

decisions.choice: angry: bitterly angry
decisions.reason: The verb is a strong one, used of bitter, lasting anger. It appears only here in the New Testament.

decisions.choice: a boy (B); a baby boy (R); a man entirely well (B); a man well in his whole body (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated word "man". Balanced and Readable say "boy" for the infant (as in 7:22) and "man" for the healed man, who is a specific adult and needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: Circumcision deals with only one part of the body
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the contrast that "whole" implies (meaning decision m3), and breaks the long question into short sentences.

decisions.choice: sané por completo (L, B); en todo su cuerpo (R)
decisions.reason: "Sano" is the word of the healing story (5:6-15). "Por completo" sets the whole person against circumcision, which concerns one part of the body (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: La circuncisión tiene que ver con una sola parte del cuerpo
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable spells out the contrast.

decisions.choice: Si l’on circoncit un petit garçon
alternatives: Si un petit garçon reçoit la circoncision
decisions.reason: French readily turns the Greek "a man receives circumcision" into the impersonal "on", which says that the rite is done to the infant (meaning decision m2) without a stiff passive. Literal keeps the Greek construction.

decisions.choice: mtu mzima kabisa
decisions.reason: Jesus refers to the man made well at the pool. "Mzima" is the word used for him in 5:6-15, so the link stays visible; "kabisa" (entirely) gives the "whole".
The same word as in the healing at the pool (5:6-15), which Jesus refers to here (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "сделал здоровым"
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up the phrase of the healing story (5:6-15, "стать здоровым"), so Russian keeps the same word.

decisions.choice: "憤る" (L, B); "腹を立てる" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is a strong one for bitter anger (m4); "憤る" carries that weight. Readable uses the everyday phrase.

alignments.target_span: what things look like on the surface

decisions.choice: do not judge: stop judging this way
decisions.reason: The present tense with "not" usually tells someone to stop doing what they are doing, or not to make a habit of it. Jesus does not forbid judging; the next clause tells them to judge rightly.

decisions.choice: according to appearance: by what is seen on the surface
alternatives: by a person's face or standing
decisions.reason: The word means what is seen. On the surface, Jesus did work on the Sabbath. Underneath, he did what the law itself makes room for, and greater.

decisions.choice: just judgment: the kind of judging the law requires
decisions.reason: Moses told Israel's judges to judge the people with just judgment, without partiality (Deuteronomy 16:18-19; Leviticus 19:15). Isaiah says the coming king from Jesse will not judge by what his eyes see but with righteousness (Isaiah 11:3-4). Jesus asks his hearers to do what their own law asks.

decisions.choice: just: right and fair
decisions.reason: The adjective describes a decision that is right and fair. It is related to the noun for righteousness but is not that key term; here it is about how a case is judged.

decisions.choice: just judgment (L); a judgment that is just (B); judge fairly ... what is really right (R)
decisions.reason: "Just" is the plain word for a fair verdict and keeps the link with Deuteronomy 16:18 (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the Greek pattern "judge the judgment".

decisions.choice: juicio justo (L); con justicia (B, R)
decisions.reason: Keeps the link with Deuteronomy 16:18 (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: jugez le juste jugement (L); portez un jugement juste (B); jugez de façon équitable (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek pattern of a verb with its own noun. Balanced uses the usual French "porter un jugement", with "Cessez de" for the force of the present command (meaning decision m1); "juste" keeps the sense of a fair verdict (m3, m4).

decisions.choice: "ቅን ፍርድ" (upright judgment, L); "ትክክለኛ ፍርድ" (right judgment, B); "በቅንነት" (fairly, R)
decisions.reason: The adjective here means right and fair judging (m4), the kind the law requires; "ጽድቅ" is kept for righteousness before God, and "ቅን", "ትክክለኛ" say fairness plainly, as the English "just" does.

decisions.choice: "उचित न्याय" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The word for a just judgment chosen in 5:30, so Jesus's own judging and the judging he asks of them use the same word (meaning decision m4).
